objects.monsterDenominatorGrading: the even unimodular Lorentzian plane II_{1,1}
objects.golayProgram: T = 1 + sigma on the cyclic binary Golay code G_23

exactJordanEmbedding.interpretation: the Monster Lie algebra grading lattice is the diagonal split plane of the full three-dimensional Jordan carrier
exactJordanEmbedding.boundary: this is an embedding of grading lattices, not a Monster action on H_2(R) and not a homomorphism from Spin_0(2,3) to the Monster

rule60GolayDecomposition.cyclotomicFactorRelation: the two degree-11 factors are reciprocal and their root exponents are the two Frobenius orbits under multiplication by 2 modulo 23
rule60GolayDecomposition.fifthPowerAction: multiplication by 5 exchanges the two Frobenius orbits
rule60GolayDecomposition.order23Interpretation: the complete 23-primary component of Rule 60 is an ordinary cyclic-shift symmetry
rule60GolayDecomposition.order89Boundary: 89 does not divide the Monster order, so T on im(T) cannot be the image of a Monster group element in a faithful action
rule60GolayDecomposition.survivingBridge: lift sigma, not T, through extended Golay, Leech and VOA data; retain T as the group-algebra polynomial 1+sigma

order23MoonshineBoundary.traceDegeneracy: the two classes have the same McKay-Thompson series
order23MoonshineBoundary.verifiedReplication: the n=2 Faber/replication identity is checked exactly through q^15
order23MoonshineBoundary.consequence: a genus-one scalar trace cannot decide which member of the 23A/23B pair a proposed lift occupies
order23MoonshineBoundary.requiredRefinement: retain lift/class data or use a twisted, defect, vector-valued or higher-genus observable

order23OrientationConvention.normalizerAction: the Sylow-23 normalizer acts by the order-11 subgroup of squares in F_23^times, producing the two QR/QNR generator orbits
order23OrientationConvention.inversion: -1 is a quadratic nonresidue modulo 23, so g and g^-1 lie in the two different Monster classes 23A and 23B
order23OrientationConvention.status: 23A versus 23B is an oriented-generator convention, not an invariant of the underlying cyclic subgroup
order23OrientationConvention.closedPart: after choosing zeta_23/QR orientation, the Golay factor selects one prime above 2 and one nonprincipal ideal class canonically
order23OrientationConvention.remainingPart: a class-sensitive defect observable may retain that choice, but no intrinsic construction can name A versus B without fixing an orientation convention

order23LeechLift.constantInterpretation: the removed +1 is the trace of the single invariant weight-one oscillator
order23LeechLift.cyclicSubgroupFact: the two order-23 Leech conjugacy classes generate conjugate cyclic subgroups and therefore have the same fixed-lattice type
order23LeechLift.boundary: the scalar identity identifies the normalized observable, not a canonical choice between the two oriented generators or a physical dynamics

discriminantMinus23OrientationGate.orientationFact: the nonprincipal pair is distinct under proper SL_2(Z) equivalence but exchanged by determinant-minus-one orientation reversal
discriminantMinus23OrientationGate.interpretation: a scalar theta trace necessarily forgets which oriented nonprincipal rail was selected
discriminantMinus23OrientationGate.survivingObservable: an oriented, chiral, defect, vector-valued or otherwise class-sensitive refinement

discriminant23Compiler.finiteFieldInput: the two degree-11 factors of Phi_23 over F_2 are indexed by the quadratic-residue and nonresidue orbits modulo 23
discriminant23Compiler.complexFourierPeriods: alpha=sum_{r quadratic residue} zeta_23^r and alphaBar=sum_{n nonresidue} zeta_23^n

primeAboveTwoRefinement.interpretation: the two Golay factors canonically select the two conjugate norm-two nonprincipal ideals once zeta_23 and the QR period alpha are declared

discriminant23Compiler.rule60ResidueInterpretation: 1+zeta_23 reduces to a primitive element of F_2048 on the selected characteristic-two rail; its order 2047=23*89 is a residue-field fact, so the factor 89 need not and does not occur in the Monster
discriminant23Compiler.lossMap: orientation/Galois conjugation exchanges the two rails while scalar theta summation identifies them
discriminant23Compiler.boundary: the finite-field-factor to oriented-ideal-class arrow is canonical relative to a chosen zeta_23; a canonical VOA lift that names the resulting generator 23A rather than 23B remains to be constructed

order23DefectChannel.latticeIdentification: this finite quadratic module is the discriminant form of U(23), the scaled Monster-Lie hyperbolic plane
order23DefectChannel.dualityCategory: Tambara-Yamagami category extending Z_23; the noninvertible duality object has quantum dimension sqrt(23)
order23DefectChannel.anomalyRestriction: the Monster anomaly has order 24, so its restriction to C_23 is zero because H^3(C_23,U(1)) has exponent 23
order23DefectChannel.interpretation: a mathematically established transition channel exchanges twist and charge rails and realizes the finite Fourier transform
order23DefectChannel.boundary: this is topological/modular dynamics inside a chiral 2D CFT, not a derived four-dimensional Hamiltonian, time coordinate or detector law

finiteTransitionSkeleton.phaseSpace: A=F_23^2 with twist-charge labels (a,b), quadratic refinement q(a,b)=a*b/23 mod 1, and standard alternating pairing
finiteTransitionSkeleton.orientationExchange: D_5:(a,b)->(5a,5^-1*b); 5 has order 22 and is a quadratic nonresidue modulo 23
finiteTransitionSkeleton.generatedGroup: dicyclic group Dic_11 of order 44 inside SL(2,23)
finiteTransitionSkeleton.meaning: D_5 exchanges the QR/QNR orientation while preserving q, and S exchanges twist and charge while reversing q; together they give a finite reversible transition skeleton
finiteTransitionSkeleton.finiteSpinAdjacency: Dic_11 < SL(2,23)=Sp(2,23) embeds as a symplectic block in Sp(4,23)=Spin(5,23), the finite Chevalley group of the same C2/B2 type as Sp(4,R)=Spin_0(2,3)
finiteTransitionSkeleton.boundary: reduction modulo 23 forgets the real signature and supplies no canonical lift to a continuous Spin(2,3) action, Hamiltonian flow or physical Wick rotation

projectiveTransitionQuotient.quotient: identify (a,b) with lambda*(a,b) for every nonzero lambda in F_23; the 528 nonzero labels become P^1(F_23) with 24 directions
projectiveTransitionQuotient.centralReduction: -I acts trivially after projectivization, so Dic_11 of order 44 descends to the dihedral group D_11 of order 22
projectiveTransitionQuotient.generatorOrientations: the 22 nonidentity powers of a chosen C_23 generator form 11 inverse pairs {g^k,g^-k}; multiplication by 5 cycles those 11 pairs
projectiveTransitionQuotient.boundary: the 1+11 count is adjacent to, but not a derived identification with, the 12 simple objects of Rep(so(3)_23) or the genus 12 of X_1(25)

genusOneChargeProjectionNoGo.input: T_{1,g^k}=T_23 for every nonzero k mod 23, because all nonidentity powers lie in 23A or 23B and those classes have the same McKay-Thompson series
genusOneChargeProjectionNoGo.consequence: untwisted genus-one Fourier projection distinguishes neutral from nonzero charge but collapses all 22 nonzero charges, so it cannot recover the 23A/23B orientation
genusOneChargeProjectionNoGo.nextAdmissibleObservable: a vector-valued/projective centralizer character, relational multi-insertion, or higher-genus sewn datum; scalar commuting insertions are exhausted by the C23 x S4 census

modularTransportReconstruction.sourceBasis: generalized-moonshine modular covariance together with Volpato's non-anomalous normalization h(V_{a,b})=ab/23 mod Z and group-like fusion
modularTransportReconstruction.exactLabelStabilizer: Gamma_1(23) modulo 23 has order 23, so its SL_2(F_23) orbit has 528 nonzero labels
modularTransportReconstruction.scalarStabilizer: the common 23A/23B Hauptmodul is Gamma_0(23)-invariant inside SL_2(Z); its modular orbit is P^1(F_23), of size 24
modularTransportReconstruction.multiplicity: each projective modular image represents 22 nonzero scalar multiples (a,b)~lambda(a,b)
modularTransportReconstruction.functionalPrescription: for each nonzero (a,b), choose gamma in SL_2(Z) whose bottom row is congruent to (a,b) mod 23 and transport T_23 by gamma; Gamma_0(23) invariance makes the scalar result depend only on [a:b]
modularTransportReconstruction.explicitMixedBranch: for a nonzero and r=b*a^-1 mod 23, T_{g^a,g^b}(tau)=T_23((tau+r)/23) in the fixed non-anomalous convention
modularTransportReconstruction.fourierProjectionRule: if T_23=sum_n c(n)q^n, then ch(V_{a,b})=sum_{n congruent ab mod 23} c(n)q^(n/23) for a nonzero; a=0 gives the neutral/charged pair already recorded
modularTransportReconstruction.moduleCharacterStatus: the scalar characters of all 529 V_{a,b} modules are functionally reconstructed: 23 product-residue types for a nonzero plus two untwisted types
modularTransportReconstruction.correction: the 529 twisted--twining entries are not 529 independent missing source functions: J supplies (0,0), while modular transport of T_23 supplies 24 scalar branches assigned to the other 528 labels
modularTransportReconstruction.remainingCalculation: compute the vector-valued/projective S4 centralizer action, retain genuinely relational multi-insertion data, or sew at genus two; the unrefined duality-defect trace and all scalar centralizer insertions are orientation-blind
modularTransportReconstruction.boundary: the reconstruction does not restore the oriented 23A/23B name, prove the conditional full dual-pair statement, perform genus-two sewing, or supply a physical carrier and detector

parafermionRefinementBoundary.sourceStatus: Honda-Kaidi-Orii arXiv v2 (24 July 2026), conditional general-p construction; Volpato arXiv v2 (11 September 2026), unconditional P(N) embedding for Fricke non-anomalous classes
parafermionRefinementBoundary.commutantInversionStatus: Volpato equation (2.33) has been executed exactly for the first three integral-grade terms of every f_[l,0] with even l; the verifier checks positivity and unit grade spacing
parafermionRefinementBoundary.defectAssemblyStatus: Volpato equations (2.52)--(2.54) are assembled through q^4 with exact Gaussian-integer phase bookkeeping; all imaginary and fractional-power residues cancel
parafermionRefinementBoundary.orientationResult: the unrefined scalar defect trace is invariant under D_5 because the reconstructed module characters depend only on ab, which D_5 preserves; it cannot name 23A versus 23B
parafermionRefinementBoundary.genusZeroStatus: X_1(25) has genus 12; Gamma_1(N) is genus zero only for N<=10 or N=12
parafermionRefinementBoundary.rankGenusCoincidence: rank Rep(so(3)_23)=12 equals genus X_1(25)=12; this numerical equality is not a derived identification
parafermionRefinementBoundary.interpretation: the class-sensitive refinement, if the stronger p=23 decomposition is completed, leaves the genus-zero Hauptmodul regime rather than producing another scalar moonshine Hauptmodul
parafermionRefinementBoundary.knownAlgorithm: derive commutant characters f_[l,t] by finite Fourier projection of the 23-twisted-twining functions and insert f_[l,0] in the published duality-defect trace formula
parafermionRefinementBoundary.missingInput: a vector-valued/projective S4 centralizer character, relational multi-insertion, or genus-two sewn amplitude tied to the corpus Golay rail
parafermionRefinementBoundary.boundary: modular transport, Fourier projection, all twelve even-l commutant seeds and the scalar duality-defect trace are now executed; the scalar trace fails the orientation test, so only a refined insertion or higher-genus record can reopen it

rankGenusSurvey.domain: odd prime divisors p of the Monster order, comparing rank Rep(so(3)_p)=(p+1)/2 with genus X_1(p+2)
rankGenusSurvey.uniqueEquality: p=23 is the unique equality in this finite Monster-prime set
rankGenusSurvey.boundary: no source or construction identifies the 12 simple defect types with the 12 holomorphic differentials on X_1(25)
